description: Nova Tech is a team of passionate young innovators who love coding, technology, and space exploration. We work together to create creative, interactive, and educational solutions using NASA data. Our goal is to make space science easier, more engaging, and accessible to everyone through teamwork and innovation.
summary:
Mars Mission is a browser-based survival strategy game that works as a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer. Players command a Mars base and must keep a crew of four alive for 30 days across three levels: Easy, Medium and Hard. Each day brings two emergency decisions, such as solar storms, dust storms, or life support failures, and every choice has a price. Players balance four resources: oxygen, power, food and radiation.

After each decision, the game shows a real NASA fact, so players learn real space science while they play. The game also pulls live solar flare data from the NASA DONKI API, and a stronger real flare increases the radiation damage in solar storm events. We built it with HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript so anyone can play it instantly in any browser, on desktop or mobile, with no installation.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Mars Mission is a browser-based game that trains young players to think like a mission commander. You lead a Mars base with a crew of four for 30 days, across three levels: Easy, Medium and Hard. Each day has two emergencies, such as solar storms, dust storms, meteor showers, fires or life support failures. Every choice has a price, so players must balance four resources: oxygen, power, food and radiation. If any resource reaches a critical level, the mission fails.

HOW IT WORKS

After every decision, the game shows what changed and a real NASA fact about that event. The game also fetches the latest real solar flare from the NASA DONKI API. For solar storm events, a stronger real flare (class M or X) increases the radiation damage. If the internet or the API is not available, the game keeps working normally. Players can save their mission and continue later.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Young learners practice decision making and resource management while learning real facts about space weather, radiation, life support, food production and communication delays. It needs no installation, runs on desktop and mobile, and is free to play, so it can be used in classrooms or at home.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

HTML5, CSS3 and vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), with no frameworks. The Web Audio API creates the sound effects and the ambient space music, so the game uses no audio files. CSS keyframe animations create the weather effects. The NASA DONKI API provides the live data. The game is hosted on GitHub Pages.

CREATIVE SIDE

The environment changes with the situation: dust storms, meteors, radiation glitches, fires, flickering lights when power is low, and an alarm glow when a resource is critical. The crew icons fade as radiation harms astronauts. Each level is harder, with bigger risks and smaller gains.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

We made the game simple for a junior audience, with short text and clear choices. We tied each event to a real NASA or partner agency source, and listed the sources inside the game in a Data Sources window. We also made sure the game works on small screens and does not depend on the internet to play.

DATA SOURCES

NASA DONKI, NASA RadLab (OSDR), Canadian Space Agency food production research, NASA Mars Trek, NASA Open APIs and OSDR.
